'''The South East Asian Mathematics Competition''' (SEAMC) is an annual three-day non-profit [[math competition|mathematics competition]] for Southeast Asian students at different grade levels. It is a qualifying competition for invitation to the [[World Mathematics Championships]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|title=Eunoia Ventures|url=https://eunoia.ventures/competition/competition_594202f68393a0.67333832|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130141439/https://eunoia.ventures/competition/competition_594202f68393a0.67333832|archive-date=30 November 2020|access-date=8 September 2021|website=Eunoia Ventures|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Competition Academy|url=http://competition.ac/competition/competition_59f041fe1b6c12.09521433|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180306202448/http://competition.ac/competition/competition_59f041fe1b6c12.09521433|archive-date=2018-03-06|access-date=11 April 2021}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=SEAMC : The S.E. Asia Mathematics Competition|url=http://seamc.blogspot.com/|access-date=2021-04-11|language=en}}</ref>

Teams have participated from China, Thailand, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Vietnam, Cambodia, and Nepal.<ref name=":1" />

Host venue locations of the SEAMC changes annually.{{Citation needed|date=September 2021}} An online version was held due to the [[COVID-19|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Southeast Asian Mathematics Competition {{!}} Guidelines|url=https://seamc.asia|access-date=2021-09-08|website=seamc}}</ref>

== Eligibility ==

* The Senior Competition is open to all students in Grade 12 (Year 13) or younger.<ref name=":0" /> 
* The Junior Competition is open to all students in Grade 9 (Year 10) or younger.<ref name=":0" /> 
* The Secondary Competition is open to all students in Grade 7 (Year 8) or younger during the month of the event and 
* Primary level for Grade 5 (Year 6) or younger.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> 

==The competition==

===History===
SEAMC is a mathematics collaboration experience for school students located in South or North East Asia to come together for 2-3 days.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}}

SEAMC was conceived of by Steve Warry, who taught at Alice Smith School in [[Kuala Lumpur]].<ref name=":0" /> He organised SEAMC in March 2001. He died one week prior to the first competition.<ref name=":0" /> Teams competed for the Warry Cup, which is named in Steve's honour.<ref name=":1" />

From 2014, the NEAMC sister event has been organised for students in Northeast Asia.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}}<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eunoia Ventures |first=Eunoia ventures |date=23 June 2019 |title=WMC |url=https://neamc.asia}}</ref> The organizers enlisted the [[Nanjing International School]] to host it initially in February 2014 with the help of Malcolm Coad.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|date=21 Mar 2014|title=South East Asian Maths Competition (2014) {{!}} Alice Smith School|url=http://www.alice-smith.edu.my/media/news/article/424/South-East-Asia-Maths-Competition-SEAMC-2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906223527/http://www.alice-smith.edu.my/media/news/article/424/South-East-Asia-Maths-Competition-SEAMC-2014|archive-date=2017-09-06|access-date=11 Apr 2021}}</ref>

In 2017, the SNEAMC family of events became the World Mathematics Championships.<ref name=":0" />

===Format===
Each school enters teams of 3 students each.<ref name=":0" /> The competition has nine rounds.<ref name=":0" />

All WMC qualifying competitions have:
* 3 days of engagement
* 9 equally weighted rounds
* 6 skills categories for prizes
* The best sum ranking across all 9 rounds win

School teams engage within the Communication skills rounds.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}}

The Collaboration skills rounds (Open, Lightning and Innovation) are in buddy teams of three.<ref name=":0" />
The Challenge are skills rounds undertaken as individuals.

Three skills rounds are (subject specific skills and procedures) knowledge based,
three are (plan and execute) strategy focused and three depend upon (new and imaginative ideas) creativity.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}}

So each strategy, creative and knowledge skill category is engaged in alone, in school teams and in buddy teams.{{Citation needed|date=April 2021}}

Past questions can be found around the web.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=SEAMC : The S.E. Asia Mathematics Competition: Past SEAMC Questions|url=http://seamc.blogspot.com/2006/09/past-seamc-questions.html|access-date=2021-04-11|language=en}}</ref>

In many SEAMC competitions, there are initial [[Icebreaker (facilitation)|icebreaker]] events.<ref name=":2" />

===Prizes===
* All participants receive a transcript of relative attainment in each of the 9 rounds.
* The highest ranked individuals in each category receive medals.
* The highest ranked individuals across all 9 rounds receive medals.
* The best ranked school team across all 9 rounds receive a respectively named Cup (for the SEAMC Junior competition, this is the original Warry Cup).{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}}
The better ranked teams across all of the competition venues that year are invited to the ultimate World Mathematics Championships showdown, hosted by [[Trinity College, Melbourne|Trinity College, University of Melbourne]] in the following July each year.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}}
